Appearance:
 Shri Bhagwan Das Verma - Advocate for the appellants/
 Shri Kamal Kumar Rochalani - Advocate appearing on be  Kekre- Advocate for respondent No.3/Insurance Company.

ORDER This miscellaneous appeal has been filed by the appellants/claimants under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, being aggrieved by the Award dated 04.04.2019 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District- Shivpuri (M.P.) (hereinafter referred to as "the Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No.333/2018, on the ground of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement thereof.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District- Shivpuri
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The date of accident, issue of negligence and the liability of the respondents are not in dispute.

The findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are not in question.
3.

As per the findings of the Claims Tribunal, due to death of Julie in the motor accident, the Claims Tribunal awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.3,70,000/- along with interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till realization.

4. Being aggrieved by the impugned award, the appellants/claimants have preferred this appeal on the ground that the learned Claims Tribunal passed the impugned award without proper appreciation of law.
It is contended that the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10663 2 MA-3764-2019 compensation awarded is on the lower side.

The oral and documentary evidence produced by the appellants clearly establishes that prior to the accident, the deceased was aged only Pappu vs Hasan Mohammad on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130447372/
1 15 years was pursuing her studies.
However, the learned Claims Tribunal failed to consider these aspects and assessed the income of the deceased only to the tune of Rs. 30,000/- per annum, which is extremely low.
Despite this, the Claims Tribunal awarded a total compensation of only Rs.3,70,000/- under all heads, which is grossly inadequate.
It is further submitted that income of the deceased must be assessed as per Minimum Wages Act of an unskilled labour at the time of accident.

It is further contended that Claims Tribunal has committed error in not awarding reasonable amount of compensation in other heads i.e. future prospects, loss of estate, loss of consortium, funeral expenses etc.
Hence, it is prayed that reasonable amount of compensation may be awarded to the claimants.
5. On the other hand, learned counsels for the Insurance Company supported the impugned award and prayed for rejection of the appeal.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.
7.
On perusal of record of the Claims Tribunal, it is found that the claimants have utterly failed to adduce any substantial evidence in regard to income of the deceased.

Hence, this Court finds it appropriate to assess the income of the deceased as an unskilled person in view of the law laid down in the cases of Sukhdevi v. Devendra Kumar, ILR 2014 MP 172; Kanwar Devi v. Bansal Roadways ,
2008 ACJ 2182; and National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Renu Devi, (2008) 3 ACC 134 in which it is held that when documentary proof of income is lacking, income is to be assessed as per the minimum wages applicable.

sentences.text: Therefore, in considered opinion of this Court, the just and proper amount of the income of the deceased as an unskilled person as per Minimum Wages Act in the present case is Rs.7,325/- per month.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10663 3 MA-3764-2019 8.

As regard to loss of income including future prospects, in the light of judgment o f National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, 2017 ACJ 2700, the claimants are entitled for loss of income including future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per Pranay Sethi (supra), future prospects @ 40% be assessed.

Further, as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, even if age of the deceased is to be taken into account, multiplier of 18 be applied.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Claimants are also entitled to get consortium in the light of the judgment passed by Apex Court in the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs.
Satinder Kaur and others reported in 2020 ACJ 2131 .

entities.text:
United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs.
Satinder Kaur and others reported in 2020 ACJ 2131
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal up to this extent be set aside and the reasonable amount of compensation be awarded adding reasonable amount of compensation under future prospects, loss of consortium,
loss of estate and other heads etc.
9.

Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to receive compensation under the following heads:-
 HEAD   Income Rs.7325 x   Future Prospects@ 40% Rs.1,23,06 Pappu vs Hasan Mohammad on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130447372/
2  After deducting Dependency 1/2 Rs.61,530/
 Multiplier 18 Rs.11,07,5  Other Heads:-
 Loss of Consortium Rs.40,000   Loss of Estate and funeral expenses Rs.30,000/
 Total Compensation = Rs.12,17,540/-
10.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation payable in the present case comes to Rs.12,17,540/- as against the sum of Rs.3,70,000/- awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal.
Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are held entitled to an additional compensation of Rs.8,47,540/- over and above the amount already awarded by the Tribunal.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10663 4 MA-3764-2019 11.
In the result, miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed.
The impugned award is modified, and the compensation is enhanced by a sum of Rs.8,47,540/-.
The aforesaid enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by Claims Tribunal from the date of deposit of Court fees by the appellants in the present appeal.
The said amount be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Rest of conditions as imposed by learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

12. In case the enhanced compensation exceeds the valuation of the appeal, the appellants shall deposit the differential Court fee (if not already paid) within a period of one month from today and furnish proof of such payment before the Registry.
Upon compliance, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of this order.
13. In view of the foregoing, the miscellaneous appeal stands partly allowed and disposed of.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *VJ*
